source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Spoon-shaped nails, cracks at the lip corners and craving for ice suggest:
questions.rationale: IDA signs: koilonychia, cheilosis, atrophic glossitis and pica.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron deficiency anemia (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: Koilonychia (spoon — shaped fingernails).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drink best helps absorption of an oral iron tablet?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C enhances iron absorption; milk, tea and antacids reduce it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron supplements (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: Vitamin C, like orange juice enhances iron absorption. Milk, tea, and antacid slow the absorption of iron.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A child is prescribed liquid iron. The nurse instructs the mother to give it:
questions.rationale: A straw prevents staining of the teeth; milk, tea and antacids reduce absorption.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron supplements (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: Oral liquid iron (elixir) should be taken with straw to prevent permanent staining of the teeth.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Iron dextran is given IM by which technique?
questions.rationale: Z-track deep IM injection prevents leakage and permanent skin staining; do not massage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron supplements (PDF p. 141)
questions.quote: Imferon is administered by Z-tract (deep 1M) method of injection to prevent permanent staining of the skin.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on ferrous sulfate is alarmed by black stools. The nurse explains:
questions.rationale: Iron salts darken stools to green or black; this is harmless. Constipation is also common.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron supplements (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: Iron salts change color of stool to dark green or black. This is expected and harmless.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The priority nursing intervention for a client with severe anemia is to:
questions.rationale: Rest reduces tissue oxygen demand, the priority in anemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Iron deficiency anemia (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: Promote rest to reduce oxygen demands of tissues. This is a priority nursing intervention.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Folic acid deficiency in pregnancy raises the risk of:
questions.rationale: Folate deficiency can cause neural tube defects such as spina bifida.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Folate deficiency anemia (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Folic acid deficiency among pregnant clients may cause congenitally acquired neural tube defects (spina bifida).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pernicious anemia results from lack of:
questions.rationale: Without intrinsic factor from gastric parietal cells, vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Pernicious anemia (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Decreased intrinsic factor production by the parietal cells of the stomach causes decreased Vitamin B12 absorption.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is most characteristic of pernicious anemia?
questions.rationale: A beefy red, inflamed tongue plus neurologic signs (paresthesia, poor balance) mark pernicious anemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Pernicious anemia (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: "Beefy" red, inflamed tongue — this is the most characteristic manifestation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Untreated pernicious anemia can cause which complication?
questions.rationale: B12 deficiency impairs neurons: paresthesia, poor balance, incoordination and cognitive changes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Pernicious anemia (PDF p. 143)
questions.quote: Neurologic involvement: paresthesia, lack of balance, uncoordinated movements

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After gastrectomy, a client needs vitamin B12 for how long?
questions.rationale: Loss of intrinsic factor is permanent, so B12 replacement (usually monthly IM) is lifelong.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Pernicious anemia (PDF p. 144)
questions.quote: Monthly vitamin B12 IM for life.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Aplastic anemia is characterized by:
questions.rationale: Bone marrow hypoplasia causes pancytopenia; chloramphenicol, toxins, radiation and viruses are causes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Aplastic anemia (PDF p. 144)
questions.quote: resulting in pancytopenia (decreased numbers of RBCs, WBCs, and platelets)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which antibiotic is known to cause aplastic anemia?
questions.rationale: Chloramphenicol can cause bone marrow suppression and aplastic anemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Aplastic anemia (PDF p. 144)
questions.quote: certain drugs (e.g., Chloramphenicol)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with thalassemia major on frequent transfusions receives deferoxamine to:
questions.rationale: Repeated transfusions cause iron overload (hemosiderosis); deferoxamine chelates iron. Watch vision and hearing.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Thalassemia major (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: Iron chelation therapy with Desferal (Deferoxamine). This reduces the toxic side effects of excess iron

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Frontal and maxillary bossing in a child with thalassemia is due to:
questions.rationale: Increased erythroid activity expands marrow cavities and thins the cortex, causing skeletal deformities.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Thalassemia major (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: These lead to skeletal deformities (frontal and maxillary bossing)

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Acute lymphocytic leukemia is most common in which group?
questions.rationale: ALL peaks between ages 2 and 9 and is often cured with chemotherapy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Leukemias (PDF p. 147)
questions.quote: ALL (acute lymphocytic leukemia) is most common in children, with peak incidence between ages 2 and 9.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a neutropenic leukemia client, which should be removed from the room?
questions.rationale: Avoid stagnant water (vases, denture cups, humidifiers), which breeds bacteria.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Leukemia: preventing infection (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Avoid exposure to all sources of stagnant water (e.g. flower vases, denture cups, water pitchers, humidifiers and plants).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A neutropenic client becomes newly restless and confused. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Mental status changes are often the first subtle signs of sepsis in neutropenia, since fever may be blunted.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Leukemia: preventing infection (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: These changes are often the first subtle signs of sepsis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a client with leukemia, which route of temperature taking is avoided?
questions.rationale: Avoid rectal temperatures, enemas and suppositories to prevent trauma, bleeding and perianal infection.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Leukemia: preventing infection (PDF p. 148)
questions.quote: Prevent rectal trauma by avoiding rectal temperature, enema or suppositories.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A lymph node biopsy shows Reed–Sternberg cells. This confirms:
questions.rationale: Reed–Sternberg cells are diagnostic of Hodgkin's disease; it presents with painless lymphadenopathy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Hodgkin's disease (PDF p. 150)
questions.quote: It is characterized by presence of Reed- Sternberg cells as detected by lymph node biopsy.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which early finding is typical of Hodgkin's lymphoma?
questions.rationale: Painless lymphadenopathy, often cervical, with fever, night sweats, weight loss and pruritus.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Malignant lymphoma (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: It is characterized by painless lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with multiple myeloma is at greatest risk for:
questions.rationale: Plasma cells activate osteoclasts, causing bone destruction, pain, fractures and hypercalcemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Multiple myeloma (PDF p. 151)
questions.quote: Severe bone pain due to bone destruction and pathologic fracture.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which urine finding is associated with multiple myeloma?
questions.rationale: Abnormal light-chain proteins (Bence Jones) appear in blood and urine.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Multiple myeloma (PDF p. 151)
questions.quote: Bence — Jones Protein in the blood and urine.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A college student with infectious mononucleosis has an enlarged spleen. The nurse teaches him to avoid:
questions.rationale: Splenomegaly risks rupture; avoid contact sports, cycling and heavy lifting.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Infectious mononucleosis (PDF p. 152)
questions.quote: avoid activities that may increase the risk of injury to the spleen (splenic rupture), such as contact sports

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child develops petechiae and nosebleeds 2 weeks after a viral illness. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: ITP often follows a viral infection in children; antiplatelet antibodies destroy platelets.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 ITP (PDF p. 153)
questions.quote: It usually follows viral infection in children.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A septic client oozes blood from IV sites and has cold, mottled fingers. Labs show low platelets and prolonged PT. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: DIC: simultaneous clotting (mottling, acrocyanosis) and bleeding (oozing), low platelets and fibrinogen, prolonged PT/PTT.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 DIC (PDF p. 154)
questions.quote: so that bleeding and thrombosis occur simultaneously

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of Mother with Complications of Childbearing
questions.stem: Which obstetric complication can trigger DIC?
questions.rationale: Abruptio placentae, eclampsia, amniotic fluid embolism and retained dead fetus can cause DIC.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 DIC causes (PDF p. 154)
questions.quote: Obstetric complications: abruptio placenta, eclampsia, amniotic fluid embolism, retention of dead fetus.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which product replaces fibrinogen in a client with DIC?
questions.rationale: Cryoprecipitate replaces fibrinogen and clotting factors; FFP and platelets are also given.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 DIC management (PDF p. 154)
questions.quote: Cryoprecipitate replaces clotting factors and fibrinogen.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug may manage mild bleeding in von Willebrand disease?
questions.rationale: Desmopressin (DDAVP) raises von Willebrand factor and factor VIII; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Von Willebrand's disease (PDF p. 155)
questions.quote: Desmopressin (DDAVP), to manage mild to moderate bleeding.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A woman with a bleeding disorder is menstruating. The nurse advises her to:
options: Use pads and track pad count
questions.rationale: Monitor pad count and saturation; avoid tampons, aspirin and NSAIDs.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 6 Bleeding precautions (PDF p. 146)
questions.quote: Monitor pad count for menstruating patient; avoid use of vaginal tampons.
